title: Béchamel Sauce (White Sauce)
description: One of the five classic French mother sauces, made with a white roux and milk to create a smooth, creamy base for gratins, lasagna, pasta dishes, and numerous derived sauces.

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Roux
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat.
Add the flour and whisk continuously for 2–3 minutes to form a smooth white roux without allowing it to brown.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Adding the Milk
steps: Gradually whisk in the hot milk, adding a little at a time to prevent lumps.
Continue whisking until the mixture is smooth and well combined.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Simmering the Sauce
steps: Add the bay leaf and clove-studded onion if using.
Simmer gently for 10–15 minutes, whisking occasionally until the sauce becomes smooth and thick.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Seasoning & Finishing
steps: Remove the bay leaf and onion.
Season with salt, white pepper, and a pinch of ground nutmeg.
For an ultra-smooth finish, strain the sauce through a fine sieve or chinois before serving.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Use as the base for lasagna and baked pasta dishes.
Mix with cheese to prepare Mornay sauce.
Serve as the foundation for macaroni and cheese or Croque Monsieur.

chefTips: Always use hot milk with a warm roux for a lump-free sauce.
Cook the roux gently without browning to preserve the classic white color.
Whisk continuously while adding the milk for a silky, smooth texture.
For a restaurant-quality finish, strain the sauce before serving.
Béchamel is the base for many classic sauces, including Mornay, Soubise, and Crème sauces.
